messages:
alex_dev: Heads-up — we're seeing a sustained ECC correctable spike in gpu-pool-usw2 starting ~02:04 UTC. Dashboards: https://dash.redwood.local/d/GPUErrors. Broad pattern: correctables rising across ~14 nodes in rack-3/4, plus intermittent Xid 13s on a subset. Baseline is ~0.5/min; current aggregated per-GPU rate ~40/min.

mira_sre: How many GPUs per node and card types? recent driver/kernel changes?

alex_dev: Mostly A100-80GB (16 GPUs/node), mixed q-sku revs. No driver or kernel rollouts in the 6h window. Temperature/power graphs look normal so far.

lina_infra: Quick grep of the logs shows repeated correctable counters and occasional Xid 13 with context switch in kernel module. Sample from node gpu-03-12:
```
[ 1097.342833] NVRM: GPU 0000:0a:00.0: RmInitAdapter() failed!
[ 1097.342838] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:0a:00): 13, PID=0a3b
[ 1097.342841] nvidia-mig: correctable ECC errors incremented: 118 -> 336
```

tim_ops: I've tentatively applied soft-drain on gpu-03-12/gpu-03-14 and pinned some high-latency traffic away from those nodes. Soft-drain = stop new allocations, let existing tasks finish. No hard-drain yet. :thumbsup:

mira_sre: Proposal for remediation flow (short-term, conservative):
1) soft-drain when per-GPU correctable >10/min sustained for 3 minutes (to catch bursts)
2) escalate to hard-drain (evacuate pods, reboot, mark for hardware tests) if correctable >20/min for 10 continuous minutes OR any Xid 13 with kernel oops
3) cooldown/hysteresis: do not re-enable scheduling for 30 minutes after hard-drain; require a successful burn-in test (30m diagnostics)
4) add a rolling window metric for 'noise_count' = sum(correctable in last 10m)

This keeps us from noisy auto-evacuations due to short-lived storms but still stops growing faults.

eva_rt: If we hard-drain 14 nodes that's ~224 GPUs offline (~7% of the US-WEST2 GPU capacity). We need fallback plan: either route to us-west-1 or use reserved spare pool (reserved pool currently has ~60 GPUs). Routing will increase cross-region egress cost and latency; flagging product teams.

alex_dev: Agreed — notify capacity/sales for potential Dedicated impact. Also want a metric estimation: if we soft-drain first, how many jobs will be delayed vs preempted? ops-sim shows ~1.2x latency for small jobs if we shift to spare pool.

lina_infra: For suspected nodes, run the following checklist before swap:
- nvml diag -> ECC counters reset test
- 30m stress run (memtest-like) under controlled env
- vendor firmware check and rollback attempt if noisy
- escalate to hardware replacement if errors persist

mira_sre: We should codify the thresholds into alert rules and a small automation lambda that performs the soft-drain action (label node: soft-drain=true) and notifies the channel with the reason. Hard-drain still requires human approval but can be auto-escalated to oncall with a single-click in Console.

ops-bot: Created incident INC-2026-4320 for gpu-pool-usw2 ECC spike. Created temp alert rule: gpu.ecc.correctable.rate > 10/min (3m) -> channel eng-infra.

tim_ops: One operational note: previously we used a hysteresis of 15m which caused flip-flopping; let's make cooldown 30m and require both node-level and rack-level aggregation before cluster-wide auto-drain to avoid cascading if a single rack is flaky.

mira_sre: Also propose to add a 'noise_score' to our node health: combine correctable rate, Xid count, and recent soft-drain events. Use score > 70 -> candidate for replacement.

eva_rt: Cost/contract note — if we move Dedicated customer workloads across regions, we need to honor data residency constraints. Marked the few affected Dedicated tenants; outreach team will coordinate.

alex_dev: Action items:
- alex_dev: draft playbook PR for the new soft->hard drain flow and noise_score (ETA: today EOD) :white_check_mark:
- mira_sre: implement alert rule changes and automation lambda (ETA: +3h)
- lina_infra: run diag+stress on the flagged 14 nodes and post results in thread (ETA: overnight)
- tim_ops: prepare capacity routing plan and customer impact note (ETA: +6h)

mira_sre: I'll also add a dashboard panel that shows node-level correctables, noise_score, and last-drain action so we can quickly triage.

alex_dev: OK let's keep this conservative for now — soft-drain automation on, hard-drain human approve, replace if burn-in fails. If we see Xid 32/45 or kernel oops escalate immediately. Thanks everyone.

lina_infra: will post node diagnostics when done. /cc @ops-oncall

tim_ops: tagging infra-rotation for awareness. :eyes:

ops-bot: Update: soft-drain automation deployed to canary pool (3 nodes) at 1852007020. Monitoring.

mira_sre: nice. once canary is stable we flip to global policy.
